title: Prepay Programme Terms for the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts
content:
Prepay is money the member pays in before the season against named product, and it is taken only inside the programme's booking window, which opens and closes on the month and day the catalogue fixes. That the request falls inside the open window is tested before the booking is taken, on the cooperative's own record of the signed request the member lodged with the agronomy desk — the kind of request it is, the stage it stands at, its own reference number and the money it asks for.

## What may be booked

The words that stood here — *"A booking must reach the programme's minimum, and the member may book no more than the programme's ceiling as a share of their input spend in the crop year immediately before the current one, because prepay is a buying commitment and not a deposit account."* — are **no longer in force** on the Crop Input Purchasing Accounts, having been superseded by the current basis on which the money the cooperative will take on a booking is worked out.

## What a booking locks

The words that stood here — *"The booking locks the price of the product it names, so the line drawn against it prices at the booked price however the list has moved by delivery."* — are likewise **no longer in force**, having been superseded by the current basis on which a delivery drawn against a booking is priced.

## Drawing the money down

Prepay is drawn down against invoices as product is taken, oldest booking first, and on programmes that allow it money booked against one input class may be drawn against another, while on programmes that do not the booking is honoured only against what it named.

## Money that stands unused

Unapplied prepay is carried forward and is forfeited to the cooperative only once it has stood unapplied for the programme's forfeiture period counted from the close of the booking window it was taken in.

Prepay is never refunded in cash on request, because the money bought product rather than credit; a member who will not use it may have it moved to another input class where the programme allows that, and where it does not, the request is one no policy settles.

## Points of judgement

**Two bookings stand on the account, one taken in October and one in November, and a delivery of the named product is taken.** The October booking is drawn first, the drawdown order being oldest booking first.

**Money was booked against seed on a programme that does not allow transfer between input classes, and the member wants it against crop protection.** The booking is honoured only against the seed it named.

**A booking stands unapplied and the forfeiture period counted from the close of that booking window has not yet run.** The money is carried forward; it is not forfeited until that period has run.

The booking window, the forfeiture period and whether a programme allows transfer between input classes are each as the member's programme shows them in the prepay catalogue insert.
